sections.title: Persona tool labels and behaviour
sections.what: Checks the Opener's Over Call is live and leads into the Lab, checks the Iceman and Closer tools are clearly illustrative, and checks the Architect and Professor tools are either open-data demos with a named source or marked as source pending.
sections.why: Keeps every persona tool honest about whether it is real, illustrative or not yet available.
sections.watch_out: Two tools are allowed to be either open-data or pending, so a silent regression to pending would still pass.

summary: Browser tests of the signature tool shown on each AI persona page, checking the tool's kind label, its heading, and its data or source note.
purpose: Confirms each persona's tool is labelled honestly: live, illustrative, demo on open data, or source pending.
why: Persona tools can look like real analysis, so each must say whether it uses real data, illustrative data or nothing yet.
how: The first test opens the Opener page, checks its tool is live, clicks through to a moment, and checks the Over Call appears in the Lab. The second test checks the Iceman and Closer tools are labelled illustrative and not a real match, with at least three table rows. It then checks the Architect and Professor tools either run as an open-data demo with a receipt naming the source, or say the source is pending. It runs an accessibility check on each.
inputs: The persona pages and their tool sections.
outputs: Pass or fail for each tool's label, heading, data table and receipt.
risks: The test accepts either open-data or pending for two tools, so it can pass while hiding that a tool has quietly stopped working.
debug: Check the tool's data-kind value and the kind label shown. For open-data tools, confirm the receipt names the expected source.
